newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 88's Morrison shares to resume.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 88's Morrison shares to resume.

text.p: Ontario and Alberta securities regulators on Thursday decided not to contest the end of a cease-trade on shares of Morrison Petroleums Ltd held by an affiliate of Canadian 88 Energy Corp.
The decision came even though Canadian 88 failed to convince regulators that its reasons for terminating a takeover bid for Morrison were genuine, the regulators said.

The Ontario and Alberta securities commissions on Monday ruled 5.7 million shares held by West Central Capital Corp would remain halted until 2359 EST (0459 GMT) Friday or until Canadian 88 provided what regulators considered a less "disingenuous" explanation for scrapping the bid.

"Staff is not satisfied further to the commission's decision," Cathy Singer, the Ontario Securities Commission's general counsel, said in an interview on Thursday. "But the cease-trade will lift tomorrow night, and we will not be seeking any further cease-trade orders."

Canadian 88 said last weekend fresh information regarding a Morrison natural gas well in southwestern Alberta revealed the company had less value than previously thought, so it withdrew the offer one day after extending it.
Morrison, which earlier on Thursday announced a friendly C$700 million merger deal with Northstar Energy Corp, said gleaning the information was impossible because it did not exist.
Singer said a news release from Canadian 88 issued late Thursday failed to satisfy regulators.

In the statement, Canadian 88 spelled out how it lent funds to West Central to buy Morrison shares before the C$652 million hostile bid was launched in early January. Canadian 88 also said it was agreed that its shareholders would receive two-thirds of any profits made if the shares were sold.
However, the information contained in the release was made public in press reports over the past two weeks.
